subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2 – Lesson 6: English in action – Shopping for food
outcomes: Use polite phrases to buy food in a shop.
Understand what Adam buys and how much he pays.

tf.why: Adam buys four oranges, not bananas.

tf.s: The shopkeeper says 'Anything else?' to ask if you want more.
tf.why: Well done! 'Anything else?' asks if you want more.

tf.s: 'Can I have six apples, please?' is a polite way to ask.
tf.why: Great! We use 'Can I have ..., please?' to ask politely.

tf.s: When you finish shopping, you say 'Can I help you?'
tf.why: The shopkeeper says 'Can I help you?'. You say 'No, that's it, thanks.'

tf.s: If 2 apples are 1 rial, 4 apples are 2 rials.

tf.why: Adam buys apples, oranges and grapes.

tf.s: 'Here you are.' is what you say when you give something.
tf.why: Correct! We say it when we give something.

boxes.q: What does the shopkeeper say first?
boxes.why: The shopkeeper starts with 'Can I help you?'.

boxes.q: How many oranges does Adam buy?
Complete: Can I ___ six apples, please?
You finish shopping. What do you say?
boxes.why: 'No, that's it, thanks' means you finish.

o: Can I have some milk, please?

boxes.q: 2 apples = 1 rial. How much are 6 apples?
How does the shopkeeper say the price?
You give money to the shopkeeper. You say...
boxes.why: We say 'Here you are' when we give something.

o: Six apples, four oranges and some grapes
mcq.why: Adam buys six apples, four oranges and some grapes.

mcq.q: What does the shopkeeper say to ask if you want more?
mcq.why: 'Anything else?' asks if you want more.
The shopkeeper says 'That's four rials, please.'
The shopkeeper asks 'Can I help you?'.

mcq.q: You want three lemons. What do you say?
o: Can I have three lemons, please?

mcq.q: The shopkeeper asks 'Anything else?'. You want some milk. What do you say?
o: Yes, can I have some milk, please?

mcq.q: Apples 2 + lemonade 1 + cereal 2 + sandwiches 4 + crisps 1 + milk 1. What is the total?
Put the dialogue in order: (a) Here you are. (b) Can I have a bag of grapes, please? (c) That's two rials.
mcq.why: First ask, then the shopkeeper gives the grapes, then says the price.

mcq.q: 2 apples are 1 rial. Sami has 3 rials. How many apples can he buy?
Why does the shopkeeper say 'Anything else?'
o: To ask if the customer wants more
mcq.why: It checks if the customer wants more food.
